items.q: What is ADHD beyond "can't pay attention"?
items.a: Poor **sustained attention** + high **impulsivity** + **time-perception/working-memory** deficits. ~**1 in 10 children** have ADHD; ~half resolve with treatment. Paradox: **hyperfocus** is possible when dopamine is high enough from enjoyment/curiosity.

items.q: How do brain networks fail in ADHD?
items.a: Healthy brains: default-mode and task networks are **anti-correlated** (seesaw). In ADHD/sleep deprivation they become **correlated**. **Dopamine acts as conductor** keeping them out of phase; the **2015 low-dopamine hypothesis** links excess unrelated neural firing to self-medication with sugar, caffeine, nicotine, cocaine.

items.q: What is an attentional blink and how do you reduce it?
items.a: Over-focusing (finding Waldo → brief celebration) makes you **miss the next target**. One session of **17 minutes** conscious **panoramic (open) gaze** training **significantly reduced** attentional blinks in a **near-permanent** way.

items.q: How are blinking, dopamine, and lateness connected?
items.a: **Blink rate is dopamine-controlled**; blinking bins time perception and resets post-blink. Low dopamine links to ADHD lateness unless deadline stakes spike dopamine. **Fixation training** (near→far stations, blink control, brief movement warm-up) improved elementary-school focus.

items.q: Can phones induce ADHD-like attention problems?
items.a: Yes — rapid in-phone **context switching** induces **subclinical ADHD**. Huberman cites limits: adolescents **≤60 min/day**, adults **≤2 hr/day**.

items.q: How do common ADHD stimulants work, and what's the long game?
items.a: Ritalin (methylphenidate), Adderall (**amphetamine + dextroamphetamine**), and modafinil raise **dopamine + norepinephrine**. Early Rx (plasticity peak age **3–12**) can teach what focus feels like; combine with behavioral training and **taper toward behavior-only** when possible. Risks: addiction, cardiovascular, sexual side effects.

items.q: Which supplement doses does Huberman flag for attention?
items.a: **DHA >300 mg/day** threshold for attention (~10 studies); **phosphatidylserine 200 mg/day × 2 months** reduced pediatric ADHD symptoms (synergy with omega-3s). Also mentioned: **Alpha-GPC 300–600 mg**; **L-tyrosine 100–1200 mg** (highly variable — caution with mood/psychiatric disorders).

items.q: Why does focus matter for life outcomes?
items.a: *"Most of the things that we get recognized for in life… are always proportional to the amount of **focus** that we can bring."* Attention = perception; impulse control = **limiting what you perceive**.
